_readme: This file is DATA, not code. The classifier reads it at runtime, so you can
add a new tracker without touching any Python. That separation is deliberate:
tracker lists change constantly, application logic does not.
1. cookie_signatures with match='exact'   - the cookie name matches exactly
2. cookie_signatures with match='prefix'  - the cookie name starts with this
3. domain_signatures                      - the cookie's DOMAIN is a known tracker
4. generic_patterns                       - regex heuristics for common names
necessary  - site cannot function without it. NO consent required (legally exempt).
functional - improves experience; site works without it. Consent required.
analytics  - measures usage. Consent required (NOT exempt, however much
marketing  - advertising, retargeting, cross-site profiling. Consent required,
Sources: vendor documentation, ICO/CNIL guidance, and the public Open Cookie
Database. Classifications are a technical aid, NOT legal advice.

cookie_signatures.purpose: Primary visitor ID. Distinguishes unique users. Default lifetime 2 years.
Per-property session state, e.g. _ga_ABC123XYZ. Suffix is the GA4 measurement ID.
Distinguishes users over a 24-hour window.
Throttles the request rate to Google's servers. Very short lifetime (~1 min).
Legacy __utma/__utmb/__utmz cookies. Their presence suggests an outdated GA install.
Session recording and heatmaps. Records how a user moves and clicks on a page.
Product analytics: per-user event tracking across a session.
Product analytics device/session identifier.
Customer data platform. Collects events then forwards them to many other tools.
Self-hosted analytics. Often chosen as a privacy-friendlier GA alternative.
Persists a Clarity user ID and session recording preferences.
Connects multiple page views by one user into a single recording.
Determines whether cookies are enabled in the browser.
Stores which link the user clicked, for ClickMap reporting.
A/B testing. Keeps a visitor in the same test variant across visits.
Browser identifier for ad delivery and conversion attribution. The single most common marketing cookie on the web.
Stores the click ID from a Facebook ad, so a later purchase can be attributed to that ad.
Encrypted Facebook ID and browser ID used for ad targeting. Set on the facebook.com domain.
Conversion linker. Carries ad-click information so conversions can be attributed.
Registers and reports user actions after viewing or clicking an ad, to measure effectiveness.
Checks whether the browser accepts cookies before ad serving begins.
TikTok Pixel identifier for ad measurement and retargeting.
Browser identifier used for advertising and platform features.
Routing cookie for LinkedIn's data centres; also used in ad delivery.
Ad ID syncing - matches LinkedIn's user ID with other ad networks' IDs.
Probabilistic browser identifier for cross-device ad targeting.
Integrates and personalises Twitter content and advertising.
Identifies unique browsers visiting Microsoft sites, for advertising and analytics.
Universal Event Tracking. _uetsid and _uetvid track sessions and visitors for Bing Ads.
__hstc / __hssc / __hssrc track visitor sessions for marketing automation and lead scoring.
Keeps a visitor's identity across form submissions, linking browsing history to a contact record.
Groups actions by users who cannot be identified by a Pinterest account.
Snap Pixel identifier for ad conversion tracking.
Reddit Pixel identifier for conversion tracking and retargeting.
Real-time-bidding identifier shared across the programmatic ad ecosystem.
Live chat widget state. The site works without it, so it is not strictly necessary.
Remembers a live-chat visitor between sessions.
Stores interface preferences for logged-in WordPress users.
Remembers the user's chosen language for internationalised routing.
Server-side session identifier. Without it a logged-in user is logged out on every page.
Java servlet container session identifier.
ASP.NET session identifier.
The __Host- prefix forces Secure, Path=/ and no Domain attribute. Reserved for security-critical cookies such as session tokens.
The __Secure- prefix forces the Secure flag. Used for authentication cookies.
Bot management. Distinguishes humans from bots. Security function, so exempt from consent.
Records that a visitor passed a challenge page, so it is not shown repeatedly.
Application Load Balancer stickiness - keeps a user on the same backend server. A textbook example of a legally exempt technical cookie.
Web application firewall session identifier. Security function.
Stores which cookie categories the user consented to. The consent record itself is necessary - you must remember a refusal in order to honour it.
Records that the consent banner has been dismissed, so it is not shown again.
Stores the user's consent state for the current domain.
Primary Chartbeat visitor identifier. Real-time readership analytics used by most large news publishers.
Chartbeat session and engagement tracking (_chartbeat2, _chartbeat4).
Chartbeat engagement-time measurement.
Records the referring page so Chartbeat can attribute traffic sources.
Piano Analytics visitor identifier.
Real User Monitoring - measures actual page performance for real visitors.
Audience measurement panel, widely used by European publishers. DeviceKey and UniqueUserIdentityCookie identify the browser.
Per-site and per-section audience measurement identifier.
Cross-publisher audience measurement identifier.
Audience measurement and demographic segmentation.
Nielsen Digital Content Ratings audience measurement identifier.
Adobe Marketing Cloud visitor ID, shared across all Adobe products on the site.
Adobe Marketing Cloud session flag.
A/B testing session identifier.
Snowplow open-source analytics visitor identifier. NOTE: despite the _sp_ prefix this is NOT Sourcepoint - a good example of why signature precision matters.
Snowplow session identifier.
Unique-device counting for Wikipedia traffic statistics.
Records last access date to count unique devices without persistent tracking. A deliberately privacy-preserving design.
In-house A/B testing framework assignment.
BBC multivariate testing - assigns the visitor to an experiment group.
BBC Echo analytics device identifier.
Sourcepoint consent management platform - stores whether the user is in a regulated region.
Identifier for the US national privacy (opt-out) consent record.
Stores the IAB US Privacy String recording the user's opt-out choice.
IAB Transparency and Consent Framework string - the user's recorded consent choices.
Google Additional Consent string, recording vendors outside the IAB list.
Records that the browser sent a Global Privacy Control opt-out signal.
OneTrust consent banner control state.
OneTrust session marker.
BBC's record of the visitor's cookie consent choices. Storing a refusal is itself necessary.
Rate-limits network diagnostic probes. Purely technical.
Data management platform identifier. Builds audience segments from reading behaviour for ad targeting.
Piano (formerly Cxense) persistent browser identifier for audience segmentation.
Piano visitor context - compressed profile of recent behaviour.
Piano user segment assignments.
Piano privacy and consent state for the Cxense ad stack.
Cxense persistent user identifier.
Cxense global user identifier, shared across the Cxense publisher network.
Cxense cross-domain identity sync cookie.
Piano paywall and audience segmentation.
Piano visitor timezone/attribute store.
Piano visitor identifier.
Piano browser identifier.
Piano browser tracking identifier.
Piano browser tracking session.
Lotame data management platform browser identifier.
Lotame data collection sync state.
Verifies that Lotame can set cookies on this domain.
Cookieless-era identity graph ID used for cross-site ad targeting.
Shared advertising identity graph ID, designed to survive third-party cookie deprecation.
ID5 third-party identity sync.
Prebid.js shared identifier passed to every ad bidder in the auction.
Criteo retargeting profile - drives 'ads for things you already looked at'.
LiveRamp identity resolution cookie.
LiveRamp Authenticated Traffic Solution envelope - a hashed-email-based identifier.
LiveRamp retry state.
Real-time-bidding user identifier shared across the BidSwitch exchange.
Cross-device identity graph - links your phone, laptop and tablet to one profile.
Programmatic advertising user identifier.
Demand-side platform bidding identifier.
Native advertising exchange user ID.
Video advertising exchange user identifier.
Ad exchange user identifier.
Ad exchange profile sync state.
Ad exchange profile data.
Ad network anonymous user identifier.
Semantic audience targeting identifier.
Programmatic ad platform user ID.
Amobee demand-side platform user identifier.
Amobee sync-domain user identifier.
Amobee partner sync identifier.
Amobee prebid consent/config cookie.
Supply-side platform user identifier.
Ad exchange user identifier synced via a partner domain.
AI advertising platform user identifier.
Contextual advertising visitor identifier.
Identity sync platform user identifier.
Behavioural retargeting and email capture - triggers popups based on browsing behaviour.
Tests whether the ad network can set cookies.
Ad platform consent state.
Ad platform device identifier.
Cross-network identity synchronisation.
Opera advertising user identifier.
Ad serving and frequency capping on publisher sites.
Google Publisher ID for personalised ad delivery.
Google ad personalisation opt-in identifier.
Ad platform user identifier.
Approximate location used to serve region-appropriate content and banners.
Stores the visitor's detected country for regional content.
Stores the visitor's detected state/region.
Cached geolocation lookup result.
BBC cookie namespace. Generic fallback - specific ckns_ cookies are classified individually above.

domain_signatures.purpose: Tag container. Itself only a loader, but it injects other trackers - treat its presence as a strong signal.
Ad click tracking and conversion measurement.
Social plugins and the Facebook Pixel.
Insight Tag for ad targeting and conversion tracking.
LinkedIn CDN, serves the Insight Tag.
bat.bing.com is the UET conversion tracking endpoint.
Retargeting - shows you ads for products you previously viewed.
Amazon's ad delivery and retargeting network.
Web font delivery. Note: a 2022 Munich court ruling held that embedding Google Fonts leaks the visitor's IP to Google and breaches GDPR - self-hosting is the safe option.
Web font file delivery. Same GDPR caveat as above.
Embedded video. Standard embeds set advertising cookies - youtube-nocookie.com is the privacy-preserving alternative.
Serves JavaScript libraries the site needs to run.
Bot protection on forms. Security function, so consent-exempt - though its data flows to Google remain contested.
Real User Monitoring for site performance.
Consent management platform - serves the consent banner itself.
BBC's own static asset and image CDN. First-party infrastructure despite the different domain.
Publisher data management platform for audience segmentation.
Audience data platform and identity sync.
Data management platform - Lotame's collection endpoint.
Adobe's data management platform - builds cross-site audience segments.
Ad traffic quality and invalid-traffic detection for Google Ads.
UK publisher advertising consortium running Prebid auctions.
Page content classification for ad targeting and brand safety.
Observed in ad-loading chains; classified as advertising infrastructure.
BBC's own analytics collection endpoint. MORE SPECIFIC than the bbci.co.uk asset entry, so it must win - see sorted_domain_signatures().
BBC first-party infrastructure (identity, APIs). Not a tracker.

generic_patterns.purpose: Matches session-identifier naming conventions such as sessionid, session_id, sess_id.
Cross-Site Request Forgery token. A security control, so consent-exempt.
CSRF token as named by Angular, Laravel and similar frameworks.
Shopping cart contents. Explicitly named as consent-exempt in EU regulator guidance.
Authentication token needed to keep a user logged in.
Stores the user's chosen language or region.
Stores a display preference such as dark mode.
Records the user's consent choice. Necessary, because you must remember a refusal in order to honour it.
